F15 / R15 differ in Au count and footprint · 26 October 2026

Scope and exact extraction

These are apparent lateral, exposed-MoS2 spectral-onset offsets in finite periodic Au-wire contacts. They are not vertical tunneling or transport activation barriers, and a size-converged bulk-like channel has not been established. The F15/R15 names are structure labels: the cells are 44.246 × 19.155 × 40 Å; Au widths are 1.5065 nm and 1.3171 nm, not 15 nm.

The original NanoDCAL atom-projected DOS is converted from Hartree and states/Hartree using 27.211383411. Mo+S weight is summed over far-core strips 0 and 15 (12 Mo + 24 S, 12 MoS2 formula units), Au excluded. Each original spectrum has 1,201 native 5 meV samples over −3 to +3 eV. No smoothing is added to the displayed raw curves; this does not assert the absence of broadening internal to NanoDCAL. Each calculation uses its own EF = 0, rather than a common vacuum alignment.

Baseline cutoff: 0.01 states/eV/f.u., with an onset sustained for 30 meV (seven samples) and linear interpolation between bracketing samples. A region whose EF PDOS exceeds the cutoff is marked unresolved, not assigned a zero barrier.

Sensitivity and validation

The 81 primary settings comprise 3 regions (far_core, far_middle, far_four) × 3 cutoffs (0.003, 0.01, 0.03 states/eV/f.u.) × 3 Gaussian sigmas (0, 5, 10 meV) × 3 persistence values (15, 30, 50 meV). The scatter plots all 81 rows without jitter; many persistence choices coincide. All 81 give a lower R15 electron offset, by 54.5–74.1 meV. This envelope represents method dependence, not a confidence interval or total physical uncertainty.

The broader 180-setting stress sweep retains the electron ordering in 177/180 settings; three small reversals are no larger than 0.491 meV. Thus the ordering must not be described as holding under every conceivable analysis choice. The Mo-only primary comparison retains the ordering in 81/81 settings; per-S absolute cutoffs are not equivalent to Mo+S formula-unit cutoffs.

Each case has 8 validated windows and 7 shared-energy boundaries. All 35,035 atomic PDOS comparisons across the 14 boundaries pass (F: 17,080; R: 17,955), worst absolute difference 7.26 × 10⁻¹⁰ states/Hartree. Source hashes, atom ordering, finite values, full coverage, checkpoint identity and manifest bindings were verified. This establishes reconstruction consistency, not k-mesh or cell-size convergence. The unchanged extraction method and results were independently recomputed.

The far-four baseline electron-onset spreads are 0.554 meV (F15) and 0.292 meV (R15). Near-EF weight continues to decay, and far-core clearances are only 12.82–13.59 Å and 13.81–14.49 Å. F15 outer-strip contamination and its 1.129–1.285 eV primary hole envelope must be retained in interpretation. No explicit SOC or many-body correction is included. Au atom count (200 versus 225), width, height, contact area and sheet deformation also differ, so no isolated shape or facet causality is established.

F10 / R10 are structure labels, not literal 10 nm widths · 26 October 2026

Previous calculation and geometry

F10 contains 96 Mo, 192 S and 150 Au atoms (438 total); R10 contains 96 Mo, 192 S and 105 Au atoms (393 total). Both cells are 44.246 × 19.155 × 40 Å, periodic along the Au wire in y. Coordinate-derived Au x widths are 1.105984 and 0.902096 nm. The original “10” naming is retained as a structure label. These cells are not literal 10 nm rods.

Original regional estimator

This summary preserves the previous analysis: sum only Mo+S PDOS over far-core strips [0, 15], normalize per formula unit, then extract the sustained cutoff onsets from that averaged spectrum. Native DOS has 1,201 energies from −3 to +3 eV in 5 meV steps. Baseline cutoff is 0.01 states/eV/formula unit, sustained for 30 meV. Original curves have no additional smoothing; exact zero samples are retained and cannot be displayed on the logarithmic axis. Each system is referenced to its own Fermi level.

The new spatial fit on later slides averages individually resolved strip onsets over [0, 1, 14, 15]. It is a different estimator and selection. In particular, its F10 hole value is approximately 1.268 eV, while the preserved original far-core estimate here is 1.276 eV. Compare all four systems using the common spatial fit table, not a mixture of estimators.

Numerical evidence

Same main settings as F15/R15: PBE-DZP, NoSpin, 300 K, 80 Ha; SCF k-grid 4×8×1; atom DOS k-grid 8×16×1. F10 converged in 33 SCF loops (density 1.9688×10⁻⁶; Hamiltonian 7.6641×10⁻⁶); R10 in 35 (2.5869×10⁻⁶ and 9.0041×10⁻⁶), below both 10⁻⁵ tolerances.

Eight F10 windows and six R10 windows passed XML completion, finite-value, energy-grid and atom-count checks. All twelve actual adjacent overlaps passed: 25,155 atom-energy values, worst absolute difference 3.796×10⁻¹⁰ states/Hartree. R10 has an independent unsplit full-range result: all 471,993 atom-energy values match the merged result, worst difference 1.484×10⁻⁹ states/Hartree. Source hashes match the merge receipts. F10’s initial unsplit DOS attempt reached its 24-hour walltime; its full merged spectrum is complete.

The 81 primary settings comprise three regions × three cutoffs × three smoothing sigmas × three onset persistence values. All give a lower R10 electron offset, by 44.3–66.2 meV. These settings measure analysis dependence, not independent statistical samples, confidence limits, or physical convergence.

Sources and limits

2026RodContact/sbh_analysis_20261024/{analysis_summary.json,barrier_summary.csv,provenance.json}; nanodcal_equilibrium_20261022/{manifest.json,latest_check.json}; dos_window_benchmark_20261023/{status_summary_20261024.json,F/merge_receipt.json,R/merge_receipt.json}. Displayed curve values and hashes are preserved in data/rod10_slide_data.json. Large raw XML/checkpoints remain excluded from Git and this presentation.

The finite periodic arrays have no demonstrated cell-size or k-mesh convergence, no explicit SOC or quasiparticle correction, and no resolved unique band edge beneath Au. Au count and geometry differ between F and R and between structure sets. These results do not isolate shape causality, establish a vertical tunneling barrier, or determine transport activation energy or contact resistance.

F15/R15: MoS₂ PDOS and fitted exposed-sheet edges

Projected over periodic y · Au excluded · native Δx ≈ 0.276 nm · each system EF = 0

Fitted exposed-sheet
spectral offsets

F15Φn = 0.165 eVΦp = 1.277 eV

R15Φn = 0.098 eVΦp = 1.357 eV

Interface band jump unresolved: MoS₂ under Au has in-gap weight.
No edges are imposed through metallic regions.

Contours interpolate 16 native strips; no extra energy smoothing.

What this figure measures

The figure projects the original Mo+S atom PDOS over the full periodic y cell, excluding all Au atoms. Each native x strip contains six Mo and twelve S atoms and is normalized per MoS₂ formula unit. It is an atomic projection, not a continuous real-space LDOS integral. There are sixteen native strips, spaced approximately 2.76 Å apart. The original energy grid is 1,201 samples from −3 to +3 eV in 5 meV steps. Contour interpolation adds no independent spatial resolution; no additional energy smoothing is applied to the displayed spectrum.

Edge estimates and fit

Native strip onsets use the established 0.01 states/eV/f.u. cutoff, a crossing sustained for 30 meV, and linear interpolation between the native bracketing energy samples. Under-Au and otherwise unresolved strips remain masked. The constant exposed-sheet fit uses the four preselected far strips [0, 1, 14, 15]; it averages their identifiable native onset energies. This differs in definition from extracting an onset after averaging spectra. The displayed values are read directly from the new spatial_analysis.json fit output, not copied from the earlier far-core analysis. Fit residuals describe within-cell spatial variation and are not confidence intervals or total physical uncertainty.

SBH versus an interface band jump

The apparent electron and hole spectral offsets are Φₙ = E꜀ − Eꜰ and Φₚ = Eꜰ − Eᵥ, referenced to each combined contact system’s Fermi level. A conduction-band step ΔE꜀ = E꜀(outside) − E꜀(under Au) is a difference between two band edges. It equals the outside Fermi-referenced offset only if E꜀(under Au) = Eꜰ is established independently. Finite in-gap PDOS does not establish that equality. A unique under-contact band edge and interface jump are unresolved in this extraction; interface_jump_eV is null. No line is fitted through the masked contact region, and no contact-edge jump is extrapolated.

These are equilibrium PBE-DZP, NoSpin exposed-sheet spectral proxies. The finite periodic wire array has no demonstrated lateral-size or k-mesh convergence. Atomic PDOS, metallic gap weight and the present fit do not establish a vertical tunneling barrier, a transport activation energy, or a contact resistance. F15/R15 differ in Au count, footprint and deformation, so the comparison does not isolate shape or facet effects. Threshold sensitivity remains relevant, especially for hole onsets.

Common spatial estimator

Every value in this table is the constant least-squares fit to individually resolved native MoS₂ cutoff onsets in fixed strips [0,1,14,15], using raw spectra, cutoff 0.01 states/eV/formula unit and 30 meV persistence. The original regional summary slides preserve onset-of-mean results, which differ from this estimator, most visibly for the F10 hole value. Spatial fit RMSE is not a confidence interval. See each spatial page’s downloadable analysis and report.

Scope of the comparison

All four cells are 4.4246 × 1.9155 × 4.0 nm. The 10 and 15 suffixes are original structure labels; Au atom-center x spans are measured directly from the POSCAR coordinates. Increasing the Au footprint also changes atom count, geometry and sheet deformation, so the observed differences do not isolate size or shape. Each calculation has its own E_F=0; no common vacuum alignment is claimed. No band step through the unresolved under-contact region is fitted.
